topic-072-pfn-fast-entropy-search-via-in.evolution: The representatives span early density-based stochastic search through budgeted Bayesian methods to large discrete scientific libraries. Recent work allocates surrogate inference across molecular partitions using bandit policies, showing that screening computation has become an explicit optimization resource.
openQuestions: How should search balance surrogate computation, evaluation cost, and uncertainty when all three change during optimization?
topic-072-pfn-fast-entropy-search-via-in.overview: Bayesian optimization chooses which expensive experiment to run next using a probabilistic surrogate of an unknown objective. This cluster studies local search, uncertainty, evaluation budgets, transfer between search spaces, and the cost of computing the surrogate itself. One representative method chooses a direction that maximizes the probability of improvement rather than simply following the expected gradient.
topic-072-pfn-fast-entropy-search-via-in.title: Bayesian Optimization and Cost-Aware Search
topic-072-pfn-fast-entropy-search-via-in.whyItMatters: When each measurement requires a simulation or laboratory experiment, a useful search policy must spend both evaluations and computation carefully. Better uncertainty handling can make limited budgets more productive without assuming that a surrogate is perfectly accurate.

topic-073-4-3-phases-of-compute-optimal-.evolution: Early representatives use statistical mechanics and linear models to study learning dynamics. Later papers examine linearized wide networks and richer infinite-width parameterizations. Recent work studies spectral separation and singular-vector alignment in deep Jacobians, with experiments restricted to settings that support the proposed approximation.
openQuestions: Which predictions from infinite-width or fixed-activation analyses remain reliable when finite networks change their activation patterns?
topic-073-4-3-phases-of-compute-optimal-.overview: This topic asks how neural networks change during optimization and why different parameterizations produce different learning behavior. The papers analyze wide-network limits, stochastic dynamics, convergence, and the geometry of Jacobians. A central distinction is whether training mainly adjusts predictions around fixed initial features or substantially learns new representations.
topic-073-4-3-phases-of-compute-optimal-.title: Neural Training Dynamics and Feature-Learning Regimes
topic-073-4-3-phases-of-compute-optimal-.whyItMatters: A convergence guarantee alone does not explain why learned features are useful. Connecting parameterization and depth to representation changes can clarify when simplified theories describe practical networks and when their assumptions exclude the behavior of interest.

topic-074-a-continuous-time-mirror-desce.evolution: Earlier representatives concern independent components, denoising, and sparse coding. Later work extends recovery to one-bit observations and unknown mixtures. Recent sparse-autoencoder research reconnects neural concept dictionaries to classical identifiability conditions, modifying architectures and training to reduce instability while improving reconstruction.
openQuestions: Which identifiability conditions can be checked on learned dictionaries rather than merely assumed?
How robust are recovered concepts when the underlying representation is only approximately sparse?
topic-074-a-continuous-time-mirror-desce.overview: Sparse recovery reconstructs signals from limited measurements by assuming that only a small number of components are active. This cluster includes compressed sensing, mixtures of sparse regressions, dictionary learning, and sparse autoencoders. The common question is when the observations determine a useful sparse representation and whether an algorithm can recover it reliably.
topic-074-a-continuous-time-mirror-desce.title: Sparse Signal Recovery and Dictionary Identifiability
topic-074-a-continuous-time-mirror-desce.whyItMatters: Good reconstruction does not automatically make a representation unique or interpretable. Recovery guarantees, robustness to imperfect sparsity, and stability across training runs help distinguish meaningful structure from arbitrary choices made by the learning procedure.

topic-075-a-3d-generative-model-for-stru.evolution: The representatives move from protein-backbone and secondary-structure prediction toward pocket-conditioned generation and conformational ensembles. Recent work emphasizes physical feedback, faster docking, and higher-order spatial relations within pockets, reflecting several complementary routes to better structural modeling.
openQuestions: How can generated candidates be evaluated beyond docking scores?
How should uncertainty over protein conformations influence molecule generation and selection?
topic-075-a-3d-generative-model-for-stru.overview: These papers use molecular and protein geometry to predict structures, sample conformations, and design candidate ligands. Methods combine learned representations with search, diffusion, flow matching, or physical feedback. A representative approach guides a genetic algorithm using neural models of protein–ligand structures, transferring information across targets before adapting during optimization.
topic-075-a-3d-generative-model-for-stru.title: Protein-Conditioned Molecular Design and Conformation Modeling
topic-075-a-3d-generative-model-for-stru.whyItMatters: Three-dimensional context can distinguish molecules that look plausible in isolation from those suited to a particular binding pocket. Computational scores and structural plausibility make screening more focused, although they do not establish biological efficacy or experimental binding on their own.

topic-076-varepsilon-fractional-core-sta.evolution: Early representatives investigate friend-or-foe learning, beliefs, and graphical games. Later work develops actor–critic and policy-gradient guarantees for richer sequential settings. Recent sum-of-squares approaches address imperfect recall, offering convergence results and tractable special cases while retaining the broader computational difficulty.
openQuestions: Which structural assumptions remain realistic when agents learn from partial observations?
Can equilibrium guarantees coexist with scalable function approximation and limited interaction budgets?
topic-076-varepsilon-fractional-core-sta.overview: Multi-agent learning must account for other decision makers whose strategies affect both rewards and future states. This cluster studies equilibria in Markov and extensive-form games, including collaboration, competition, and imperfect information. Methods combine policy learning with optimization tools that exploit special game structure rather than assuming arbitrary games are easy to solve.
topic-076-varepsilon-fractional-core-sta.title: Equilibrium Learning in Sequential Multi-Agent Games
topic-076-varepsilon-fractional-core-sta.whyItMatters: An individually improving agent can destabilize a learning system when opponents also adapt. Equilibrium guarantees clarify what collective behavior an algorithm targets and how much interaction or computation it may require under stated assumptions.

topic-077-voice-benchmarking-full-duplex.evolution: The representatives extend from early speech and music learning to text-conditioned diffusion and instruction-based audio editing. Recent work includes streaming spatial audio and full-duplex agent benchmarks. These benchmarks separately examine task completion and conversational behavior, revealing capability gaps that clean synthesis evaluations would miss.
openQuestions: How can generation quality, interaction timing, and task reliability be evaluated together?
What representations support precise editing without changing unrelated audio content?
topic-077-voice-benchmarking-full-duplex.overview: This topic brings together audio synthesis, editing, segmentation, and spoken interaction. Generative methods learn compact audio representations and connect them to text or other conditions, while interactive systems must coordinate listening, speaking, and task execution. One diffusion approach addresses scarce paired data through prompt enhancement and generation in a spectrogram-derived latent space.
topic-077-voice-benchmarking-full-duplex.title: Controllable Audio Generation and Interactive Speech Systems
topic-077-voice-benchmarking-full-duplex.whyItMatters: Producing convincing sound is only one requirement for useful audio systems. Users also need controllable content, responsive timing, and reliable behavior amid accents, noise, interruptions, and multi-turn tasks.

topic-078-mathcal-m-4-a-unified-xai-benc.evolution: Early representatives concern learning from and reusing explanations. Later work focuses on neural attribution and training models to respect explanatory constraints. Recent studies extend sufficiency tests to language-model explanations and show that conclusions depend on the input distribution used to evaluate them.
openQuestions: How should an explanation's evaluation distribution be chosen?
When does optimizing explanation quality improve the underlying decision process rather than just its presentation?
topic-078-mathcal-m-4-a-unified-xai-benc.overview: Explainable learning aims to show which information drives a model's prediction and to make those explanations useful. This cluster includes feature attribution, self-explaining architectures, explanation regularization, and free-text rationales. A representative method lets practitioners penalize inappropriate feature importance, turning an explanation into a training signal informed by domain knowledge.
topic-078-mathcal-m-4-a-unified-xai-benc.title: Faithful Explanations and Explanation-Guided Learning
topic-078-mathcal-m-4-a-unified-xai-benc.whyItMatters: An explanation can sound plausible without faithfully describing the model. Evaluating stability, sufficiency, and sensitivity to relevant inputs helps separate persuasive descriptions from evidence that supports correction or understanding.

topic-079-a-flexible-framework-for-nonpa.evolution: The representatives progress from conditional density estimation and multivariate factorization to nonparametric graphical and latent-variable models. Recent work learns spectral representations for conditional-independence testing, linking representation error to statistical validity and power rather than treating learned features as automatically trustworthy.
openQuestions: How can flexible dependence models scale while retaining calibrated uncertainty?
Which representation-learning errors most threaten the validity of conditional-independence tests?
topic-079-a-flexible-framework-for-nonpa.overview: This cluster studies relationships among variables without requiring a simple joint distribution. Copulas separate marginal behavior from dependence, graphical models encode conditional relationships, and latent-variable methods explain shared variation. One representative approach uses Gaussian processes to let conditional copula shapes vary with the variables being conditioned on.
topic-079-a-flexible-framework-for-nonpa.title: Flexible Dependence Modeling and Conditional Independence
topic-079-a-flexible-framework-for-nonpa.whyItMatters: Incorrect dependence assumptions can distort uncertainty estimates and obscure which variables supply independent information. Flexible models and valid conditional-independence tests support statistical modeling, feature selection, and causal analysis, while still requiring explicit assumptions for their guarantees.
